correctness.rationale: Every Eulerian circuit of the binary four-bit de Bruijn graph induces one of 65536 local pairings; one 32-cycle produces exactly one rotation class once edge 00000 is fixed as origin. Independent DFS enumerates the same set of 2048 words. Both distinct correct LZ76 parsers agree for each of 65536 rooted strings. Direct assertions of all four rooted multiplicities and all four cyclewise (minimum,maximum) multiplicities, plus arithmetic consistency, pass in verify.py. Finite completeness is mathematically established, not extrapolated.

value.rationale: The exact interaction of cyclic de Bruijn universality with the linear, orientation-sensitive LZ76 exhaustive history is a natural finite combinatorial statistic. Full rooted distribution and joint cut extrema for every order-five cycle reveal nontrivial cut dependence despite identical length-five circular factor sets. Unlike a bare score of one chosen representative, the minimum–maximum law classifies every cycle, providing reproducible reference data for universal-cycle phrase complexity. The order-five size and no-all-order limitation are explicit; the claim is not presented as an asymptotic compression theorem.
